name: Slovakia
summary: White, blue and red horizontal bands with the coat of arms toward the hoist: a white double cross on red, standing on three blue hills. The tricolour dates from the revolutions of 1848.
origin: Slovak nationalists adopted the white-blue-red Pan-Slavic tricolour in 1848. It was used by the First Slovak Republic (1939–1945), a client state of Nazi Germany.

After the Velvet Revolution, Slovakia adopted the tricolour with the coat of arms on 1 September 1992, before the dissolution of Czechoslovakia on 1 January 1993. The arms were added partly to distinguish the flag from Russia's.

symbols.name: Double cross
symbols.description: A white double-barred cross on red.
symbols.meaning: Christianity; traced to the Byzantine mission of Saints Cyril and Methodius to Great Moravia in the 9th century.

symbols.name: Three hills
symbols.description: Three blue hills beneath the cross.
symbols.meaning: Commonly identified as the mountain ranges Tatra, Fatra and Mátra.

facts: Hungary's arms also feature a double cross on three hills, reflecting shared history.
The Mátra range is now in Hungary.
Slovenia's flag is often confused with Slovakia's.
clues: White, blue and red bands with a shield showing a white double cross on blue hills.
Its three hills are traditionally named after three mountain ranges.
Adopted months before its federation split peacefully in 1993.
